bugs.summary: R_realloc(): resizable R_alloc()-style transient memory that preserves vmaxget() marks

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
On bug 19208 Luke suggested an R_realloc() so that a buffer grown with R_alloc() does not keep every superseded block alive until the call returns. This adds it.

    char *R_realloc(void *p, size_t nelem, int eltsize);

R_realloc(NULL, n, size) allocates a block that is used like one from R_alloc(); passing it back resizes it, keeping the contents up to the smaller size. A same-size request is a no-op, a zero size shrinks to a minimal block (never NULL, so the pointer and its stack position stay usable), and an allocation failure leaves p valid. Only blocks from R_realloc() can be resized; R_alloc() blocks are rejected.

The design goal is that saved vmaxget() marks, including those held by R_ToplevelExec() and R_UnwindProtect() contexts, stay valid across a resize. R_alloc() is untouched and pays nothing: a vector linked through ATTRIB on R_VStack as before. A resizable block instead sits in the CAR of a CONS_NR node on the same chain, with its ATTRIB pointing back at the node. Resizing allocates the new vector and SETCARs it into the node, so the superseded vector is garbage at once while the node, and hence every mark, stays where it was; nothing is ever unlinked. The node is found from the block header in O(1) by checking that ATTRIB(block) and CAR(node) point at each other rather than by walking the stack, which goes quadratic once allocations pile up above the buffer (12 s against 0.1 s for 1e5 grows with one R_alloc() per step). A foreign pointer is rejected when the memory before it does not look like a resizable block; the manual calls this best-effort.

The patch (r-realloc.diff, against r90650):

- memory.c: R_alloc() split around a size helper, no behaviour change; R_realloc() and its node lookup.
- R_ext/Memory.h: the declaration.
- R-exts (Transient storage allocation) and R-ints (R_VStack), with cross-references to the unrelated malloc-based R_Realloc macro; NEWS.
- tests/R-realloc.c and R-realloc.R: an R CMD SHLIB test run by a new test-Realloc target (check-devel, Makefile.install{,.win}, testInstalledBasic("devel")), skipped when no compiler works. It covers contents and marks across grow/shrink/regrow of buried blocks, R_ToplevelExec()/R_UnwindProtect() with and without an error unwind, every error path including foreign pointers, and reclaimed memory as measured by gc(), all repeated under gctorture(TRUE).

make check passes in a normal build; test-Specific and test-Realloc pass under --enable-strict-barrier. 2e7 small R_alloc() calls time the same as trunk.

The readLines() buffer from bug 19208 is the obvious first user; I have kept that out of this patch so the two can be considered independently.

Also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/366, where CI results can be seen.

patch v2: R_realloc() with misuse checks, manual text and tests, against r90650

Updated patch (r-realloc.diff, still against r90650): R_realloc() now reports a pointer superseded by an earlier resize distinctly, and under PROTECTCHECK vmaxset() checks that the restored position is on the stack and empties the released nodes, so resizing a released block is an error instead of a use of collectable memory. The default build is unchanged; VALGRIND_LEVEL > 1 marks the superseded block inaccessible. Also in https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/366.
